sources.used_for: Section 5 requires the exact statement 'As an Amazon Associate I earn from qualifying purchases.'; Section 1 defines Special Links and the tagged-link requirement. || VERBATIM RE-READ 2026-11-20 (session 66f2548a): §5 requires the site to state clearly and prominently "As an Amazon Associate I earn from qualifying purchases.", and bars misrepresenting or embellishing the relationship "including by expressing or implying that we support, sponsor, or endorse you". §6 provides that "any violation of Section 5 and as specified in the Program Policies will be deemed a material breach of this Agreement", so a missing or buried disclosure is a termination-grade defect rather than a style preference. §4 states "We do not make any representation, warranty, or covenant regarding the amount of traffic or commission income you can expect at any time", the official basis for publishing no revenue forecast, conversion score or traffic estimate anywhere in this repository.

sources.title: Associates Program Policies (Commission Income Statement, Participation Requirements, IP License, Trademark Guidelines)
sources.used_for: Participation Requirements §2(a)-(b): Special Links must carry the Associates tag as a URL parameter and must be accessed directly from the site. §2(b) price clause: a site may show price and availability only if Amazon serves that data or it comes from the Creators/PA API. Also the anti-misleading-claims clause and the trademark rules. || VERBATIM RE-READ 2026-11-20 (session 66f2548a), closing the earlier excerpt caveat on §2 and recording clauses not previously read: · §2(a) "Special Links must use the Associates ID we have assigned to you." · §2(b) "you must include your Associates ID or 'tag' (appearing as XXXXX-##, or such other format as we may designate) as a parameter in the URL of each link you place on your Site to an Amazon Site." · §2(b) bars bookmarking Special Links and requires direct access from the Site; bars inaccurate, overbroad, deceptive or misleading claims about any Product; requires removing links and references to a limited-time promotion as soon as it ends; requires additional original content when linking to Product lists. · §3(b) makes the Associate responsible for disclosures "for example, if applicable, the U.S. FTC Guides Concerning the Use of Endorsement and Testimonials in Advertising". · §3(e) requires disclosing "either through a privacy policy or otherwise, the use of cookies, pixels, and other technologies by you and third parties and how you collect, use, store, and disclose data collected from visitors". · §4 permits Special Links in email, SMS and direct messages only where solicited and opted into. · §5 bars using Special Links or Program Content "to develop machine learning models or related technology" without express prior written approval (FLG-031). · §6(b) bars tag-formatted links on a site that is not your Site. · §6(g) bars any consideration, reward or incentive for using Special Links. · §6(s) bars artificially generating clicks or impressions. · §6(t) bars displaying customer reviews or star ratings without the Creators API or PA API. · §6(u) bars purchasing through your own Special Links, so gate G-02 must be tested against the tracking report and never by placing an order. · §6(v) bars cloaking or obscuring the URL containing Special Links including by Redirecting Links. · §6(w) bars a link shortener used "in a manner that makes it unclear that you are linking to an Amazon Site" - the clause turns on clarity of destination and does not ban shorteners as such. · §6(y) "Unless otherwise agreed by Amazon, your Site must not have price tracking and/or price alerting functionality" (FLG-032). · Preamble: any violation of the Participation Requirements, the IP License or Influencer Program Policy §1 is a material breach. · Commission Income Statement §1: the Session ends at the first of 24 hours elapsing, an order placed for a non-digital Product, or a click through someone else's Special Link; cart additions count 89 days; ship and pay within 180 days. sources.title: 16 CFR 255.5 - Disclosure of material connections
sources.used_for: Why the disclosure sits above the fold on every page: a material connection must be disclosed clearly and conspicuously, and an affiliate commission is a material connection (Example 11).
sources.quote: When there exists a connection between the endorser and the seller of the advertised product that might materially affect the weight or credibility of the endorsement, and that connection is not reasonably expected by the audience, such connection must be disclosed clearly and conspicuously.

sources.title: 16 CFR Part 255 - Guides Concerning Use of Endorsements and Testimonials in Advertising (full part)
sources.used_for: The rule that the disclosure must be in the same place as the endorsement, not buried on a separate page.

sources.title: Google Search spam policies (including scaled content abuse and site reputation abuse)
sources.used_for: The reason this site publishes a small number of hand-checked pages rather than auto-generated pages at scale, and the reason every page has a named publisher and a contact route. Google lists affiliate links used throughout a page, with links qualified properly, among practices that are not inconsistent with its site reputation policy.
